sections.heading: Before you drive — C
sections.markdown:
FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A09
Ohio prohibits operating or knowingly allowing a vehicle on a highway when its unsafe condition endangers anyone. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A09
A vehicle must not carry protruding objects, sharp broken edges or parts that could injure someone touching them. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A10
The steering mechanism should work normally without excessive looseness at the steering wheel. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A10
Vehicle tires need at least one sixteenth of an inch of tread and must have no major bulges, bumps or damage. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A10
An average motor vehicle should have at least two safety belts in its front seat. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A10
The service brake must provide enough braking to slow, stop and control the vehicle. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A10
The parking brake must be capable of keeping the vehicle stationary on a slope. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A10
A vehicle should have two functioning headlights, with one mounted on each side. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A10
The vehicle should have two red rear reflectors that can be seen from three hundred feet. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A10
At least one red taillight should be visible from five hundred feet. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A10
The vehicle should have two red brake lights visible from five hundred feet when braking. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A10
A white lamp should make the rear license plate visible from fifty feet. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A10
Working turn signals should include two front signals and two rear signals, visible from three hundred feet. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A10
Windshield wipers must function well enough to remove precipitation from the windshield. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A10
The rear-view mirror should give the driver a clear, unobstructed view behind the vehicle. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A10
A functioning vehicle horn should be recognizable as a motor vehicle horn and audible from two hundred feet. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A10
The exhaust system should remain in good working condition and operate continuously. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A10
The windshield light-transmission standard stated in the handbook is seventy percent. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A10
The handbook allows fifty percent light transmission through front-seat side windows, with a tolerance of three percentage points in either direction. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A10
Use the vehicle identification number to search the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration website for safety recalls. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A10
Too little air, too much air or insufficient tread in a tire can create road-safety problems. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A11
Use the vehicle maker's recommended tire pressure shown on the door jamb. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A11
Measure tire pressure when the tires have reached the temperature of the surrounding air. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A11
To measure tire pressure, take off the valve-stem cap and apply a pressure gauge. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A11
Add air when tire pressure is below the recommended level, or let air out through the valve when pressure is above it. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A11
For a penny tread check, put Lincoln's head into the deepest tire groove; seeing his entire head means the tire is too worn to drive on and needs replacement. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A11
Ohio permits studded tires from November first through April fifteenth. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A11
Use headlights between sunset and sunrise, when visibility is poor, and whenever precipitation requires windshield-wiper use. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F29 | anchor: A11
High beams may be used while headlights are needed, except when a vehicle is approaching from the opposite direction. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F30 | anchor: A11
Use turn signals to announce a turn, a change in direction or a lane change on a road with multiple lanes. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0011]

sections.heading: Before you drive — C2
sections.markdown:
FACT_ID: sec01-R01 | anchor: A11
Start the turn signal at least one hundred feet before changing direction. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R02 | anchor: A11
Hazard lights help others see a vehicle that has stopped on the roadway or nearby. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R03 | anchor: A11
Sit upright with your back supported by the seat and your feet on the floor. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R04 | anchor: A11
Before moving, position the seat for a clear windshield view, full pedal and steering control, and enough room for air-bag deployment. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R05 | anchor: A12
A properly positioned seat lets your foot pivot easily between brake and accelerator while your heel stays on the floor. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R06 | anchor: A12
With the seat correctly adjusted, the steering-wheel top is no higher than your shoulders and remains below your chin. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R07 | anchor: A12
Keep at least ten inches between your chest and the steering wheel to provide space for air-bag deployment. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R08 | anchor: A12
Position the head restraint against the back of your head, at least as high as your ears, to help prevent whiplash. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R09 | anchor: A12
Set the mirrors before driving so they provide the best available view beside and behind the vehicle. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R10 | anchor: A12
Aim the interior rear-view mirror to frame the rear window and show traffic behind you. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R11 | anchor: A12
For the left outside mirror, rest your head against the closed driver-side window and adjust until only a small part of the vehicle's left edge remains visible. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R12 | anchor: A13
For the right outside mirror, lean until your head is over the center console, then adjust until the rear edge of your vehicle is barely visible. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R13 | anchor: A13
The described outside-mirror adjustment adds twelve to sixteen degrees of view on each side, although the vehicle's sides are no longer visible in a normal mirror glance. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R14 | anchor: A13
With the described mirror adjustment, a vehicle behind moves from the inside mirror to an outside mirror, then into the driver's peripheral view. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R15 | anchor: A13
Air bags supplement safety belts and work best together with them to reduce the chance of the head or upper body striking the interior in a crash. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R16 | anchor: A13
Consult the vehicle owner's manual for information specific to its air bags. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R17 | anchor: A13
Drivers and front-seat riders in most passenger vehicles must wear safety belts on Ohio roads, including vehicles equipped with air bags. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R18 | anchor: A13
Fasten your own safety belt and check that every passenger uses a safety belt or a child restraint. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R19 | anchor: A13
For a driver younger than eighteen, occupancy cannot exceed the number of originally installed safety belts, and every occupant must wear one. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R20 | anchor: A13
Place the safety belt over the body's bony shoulder and hip areas. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R21 | anchor: A13
Wear the shoulder belt over the shoulder and chest with little or no slack, never under an arm or behind the back. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R22 | anchor: A13
Incorrect shoulder-belt use can cause serious internal injury during a crash. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R23 | anchor: A13
After fastening, tighten the lap belt so it sits low and snug across the hips. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R24 | anchor: A13
A poorly positioned lap belt can let you slide out during a crash, causing injury or death. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0013]

Confusables: service braking controls motion; parking braking holds a parked vehicle. Hazard lamps identify a stopped vehicle; turn signals communicate a planned change. Air bags supplement belts. Mnemonics: check, adjust, fasten. Glossary: tread is the tire surface measured in the cited tire checks; interior and outside mirrors have different viewing roles. These labels organize the cited facts and add no new driving rule.
